series.title: What Does It Take To Have A Successful Marriage?
series.description: In Genesis 2:24, God declares that a man shall leave his father and mother, hold fast to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh. Yet today, we witness countless divorces, separations, and marriages sustained by unhealthy forbearance. Why? What does it truly take to build a successful marriage? Could the answer lie in a foundation we often overlook - honesty?

episodes.title: What Does It Take To Have A Successful Marriage?

sections.heading: God's Design for Commpanionship
message: From the beginning, the Bible tells us that it is not good for man to be alone.

Throughout creation, after God created something, ytHe declared it good. In Genesis 1:31, God looked at everything He had made and declared it very good. Yet Genesis 2:18 reveals something significant: God said it was not good for the man to be alone.
This was not a contradiction. Genesis 2 takes us into the process of creation, before the companionship God intended for humanity had been established.
From the beginning, human beings were created for relationships and community, not isolation.

sections.heading: A Suitable Helper, Not a Subordinate
message: God Declare that He would make a suitable helper for Adam.

The Hebrew expression ezer kenegdo, often translated as "suitable helper" carries a deeper meaning than the English word "helper" might suggest. It describes someone corresponding to him, a counterpart, an ally, someone suited to stand alongside him rather than someone of lesser worth.

The foundation of marriage in Genesis recognizes the spouse as a partner of equal human worth and value. marriage was not designed around one person's humanity being more important than the other's. It was establisshed as a relationship of companionship and shared life.

sections.heading: Leaving and Becoming One
message: The bible tells us that a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh.
Here, we see the establishment of boundaries.

marriage creates a new family relationship in which the spouse becomes the primary partner taking priority over parents, siblings, and other outside relationships. This does not mean abandoning family or cutting every other relationship. It means establishing an independent household where the couple makes decisions together without allowing outside relationship to govern their marriage.
The couple must recognize that their marriage is now a shared responsibility.

sections.heading: Are communication, commitment, and Intimacy Enough?
message: When people discuss successful marriages, they often mention commitment, communication, respect, emotional intelligence, and intimacy.

These are all important. But are they enough?
We know people who communicate exceptionally well. We know people who are respectful, emotionally intelligent, self-aware, and capable of understanding others. Yet these qualities do not automatically produce a successful marriage.

Communication, for example, does not necessary mean honesty. Two people can communicate regularly while withholding the truth. Someone can express feelings clearly while concealing intentions. A person can be respectful and still avoid acknowledging what they truly want. These qualities help sustain a relationship, but they raise a deeper question which : What must exist for these qualities to operate genuinely?

sections.heading: Honesty Before Commitment
message: One of the foundational pillars of a successful marriage is honesty. Not simply honesty with the person we are marrying, but honesty with ourselves.

Honesty allows two people to know from the beginning what they are entering, how they intend to approach it, what they can offer, and what they cannot accept. It allows us to be ourselves without permitting emotions, temporary feelings, or particular moments to pressure us into telling someone what they want to hear.
sometimes, because we love someone or fear losing them, we make promises that do not reflect who we truly are. we agree to things we know we cannot comfortably accept.
